names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Ιανουαρίου, «Όσιος Αλέξανδρος ο Ακοίμητος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 3. јул ст. ст., „Преп. Александар“ — „Преп.“ is the rank and comes off, and the heading gives nothing else at all: no by-name, no see, no place. **The fold is deliberate and it is the deepest of this range**: `foldchk.py` returns `alexander-companion-of-antonina`, `alexander-companion-of-thalaleus`, `alexander-of-alexandria`, `alexander-of-cartagena` and `alexander-of-side`, all `sr`, for «Александар», so this is the **sixth** folder on the string. There is nothing in the heading to break it with — «the Sleepless» of the display name is the corpus’s own rendering of saint.gr’s Ακοίμητος, and „Неусипајушчих“ in the body names the monastery and not the man. A by-name is kept only where the heading itself gives one, which is the 18 June rule applied in the direction that costs.

The calendar’s nominative from name link 112, «Преподобный Александр Константинопольский», with the rank word at the head left off. The day’s own line gives the name in the genitive with the monastery instead of the city. `fk.mjs` returns no other holder for the form.

death.note: saint.gr's own header prints «Οσιος Αλεξανδρος ο Ακοιμητος (; - 430)»; the page's text says only that he fell asleep in peace.

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, and this folder’s man beyond doubt: the line names him the first founder of the monastery of the Unsleeping Ones, which is the epithet this folder’s display name carries, and gives «ок. 430», about 430, which is the year the folder already holds off saint.gr. `dates` unchanged. THE DAY IS THIS FOLDER’S SERBIAN DAY AND NOT ITS GREEK ONE: its Serbian row keeps him on the Julian 3 July and its Greek row on 15 January, and this row joins the Serbian. Name link 112 gives him the epithet «Константинопольский». The life index id112 WAS NOT OPENED. The day page prints no hymn under his name.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Ιανουαρίου — «Όσιος Αλέξανδρος ο Ακοίμητος»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 16.07.2026 (3. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. Александар“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **TWO CALENDARS, TWO DAYS, AND NO §4 NOTE IS OWED BY THIS ROW.** This folder’s only other venerated row is the Greek one, on **15 January**, and this book keeps him on the Julian 3 July — a different menologion number altogether, not a thirteen-day conversion of it. §4’s second-day note belongs on a row of the **same** church that is already `venerated`, and this folder’s `serbian` row was `undocumented`, so the row is written plainly on the day this book gives and **nothing of the Greek row is touched** — the two days are recorded here side by side, exactly as this corpus already records them on `photius-of-kyiv`, whose Greek row keeps 2 July and whose Russian row keeps 16 September. **THE IDENTIFICATION, MADE ON THE SCENE AND NOT ON THE NAME.** «Александар» is a fold five folders deep and the heading gives one word, so the name decides nothing. The body decides it: born in Asia, schooled in Constantinople, an officer by profession, who read the Saviour’s words in Matthew and sold all he had; and then „установио Обитељ Неусипајушчих“ — he founded the Monastery of the Unsleeping, whose brethren were divided into **24 чреде**, twenty-four turns, each knowing its own hour of the day or night and going into the church to continue the reading and chanting of the turn before it, so that the service ran day and night without a break. That is this folder’s whole reason for existing: saint.gr’s page explains the name Ακοίμητος in those very terms, the monks «divided into groups, praising God in succession through the whole of the day and the night, so that prayer never once stopped». The year closes it: he ended his earthly life „у Цариграду 430 год.“, at Constantinople in the year 430, and the folder already holds `death` 430 off saint.gr’s header «Οσιος Αλεξανδρος ο Ακοιμητος (; - 430)». **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE AGREEMENT IS WHY.** Two books, one year, no disagreement to widen and nothing to add: the field is passed back verbatim, note and all. This book adds the **place** of the death, which saint.gr did not give — and a place is not a date, so it goes in the life and into no field, and into no `locations` either, a city named in a narrative not being a coordinate. WHAT IS NEW, IN A FOLDER WHOSE LIFE SAYS OUTRIGHT THAT IT DOES NOT ATTEMPT HIS LIFE. Almost all of it. saint.gr’s account the folder declined to copy is replaced by this book’s: the birth in Asia, the schooling in Constantinople, the military service and the commission; the reading of „Aко хоћеш савршен да будеш, иди продај све што имаш и подај сиромасима, и имаћеш благо на небу, па хајде за мном.“ with its reference (Мат. 19, 21) and the selling and giving away of everything; the withdrawal into the desert; the long ascesis before the foundation; the twenty-four turns and the unbroken office; the travelling through the eastern parts with nothing at all, the enlightening of men, the disputing with heretics, the wonders; the growing old in the Lord’s service; and the relics at Constantinople showing a wonderworking power. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND **`soldier` AND `wonderworker` ARE BOTH REFUSED**. `venerable` and `abbot` are both there; „Преп.“ is the `venerable` and the founding of a monastery with its own rule is the `abbot` the folder already carries. „постао официр“ — he became an officer — and „чинио чудеса благодаћу Божјом“ — he worked wonders by the grace of God — **both stand in the body**, where the heading gives only Преп., and a rank read off a body is not written. No `office`. **No rows**: the monastery is not a person, the heretics he disputed with are unnamed, and the Gospel he read is not a folder. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FOURTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE NEAREST NAME IS REFUSED ON THE DOUBLE-COMMEMORATION RULE. „Преп. Исаија Отшелник“ — Isaiah the hermit, who struggled in the Egyptian Scetis in the fifth and sixth centuries, is mentioned in the book of Barsanuphius and John (answer 249 and others) as a man of particular holiness, wrote many instructions for monks and hermits, of which little survived and much was destroyed by the Muslims, and whose sayings on the mind before it wakes from the sleep of sloth, on the sign that a sin is forgiven, and on the crown of the virtues being love fill most of the entry. **No folder holds him, and eight folders begin with his name.** `ls saints | grep -i '^isaiah'` returns eight: `isaiah-the-prophet`, who is the Old Testament prophet; `isaiah-of-rostov`, `isaiah-of-the-kyiv-caves`, `isaiah-of-valaam`, `isaiah-of-peking` and `isaiah-of-kykkos`, none of them an Egyptian; `isaiah-companion-of-terentius`, one of a company; and `isaiah-the-egyptian`, whose epithet is the trap. **`isaiah-the-egyptian` is not this man and may not take this row.** His `types` is `martyr`, his `death` is 284 to 305 off saint.gr’s reign of Diocletian, and he is one of the twelve martyrs of Caesarea in Palestine listed with Pamphilus — three centuries before a hermit of the fifth and sixth, and a martyr rather than a writer of instructions. **And he already carries a venerated `serbian` row, on the Julian 16 February**, read off this same book’s entry for the twelve. Two commemorations on one calendar means two men, which is how the Prologue’s Egyptian monk Дула was kept off `doulas-of-cilicia` on 15 June, and it settles this one the same way. `grep -ril scetis saints/` returns fifteen folders and **not one of them is an Isaiah**. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth and sixth centuries are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. `barsanuphius-the-great` exists and **takes no row**: the book that mentions Isaiah is a citation and not a kinship, and the entry it would hang on is refused in any case.
